## ed658816cdb6

**Reproduced teaching defect: undeclared distance-metric shortcut.**

The rule keeps the colored blob with minimum point-to-blob Manhattan distance from a color-9 anchor. I tested the plausible rival “minimum squared Euclidean point-to-blob distance.” The rival fits all 3/3 canonical pairs.

A production-lawful lesson from seed 0, difficulty `easy`, sample indices `[7,8,9,10]` uses three consecutive demonstrations and one query. All four inputs pass the generator's `self_check`. The rival matches the selected Racket output on all three demonstrations but differs on the query (`checks/audit/ed658816cdb6/probe.json`).

On the query, the anchor is `[3,5]`. The color-4 blob has minimum Manhattan distance 3 and squared Euclidean distance 9; the color-3 blob has Manhattan distance 4 and squared Euclidean distance 8. The selected Racket rule therefore keeps color 4, while the rival keeps color 3. Inputs, selected-authority outputs, and rival outputs are retained in:

- `checks/audit/ed658816cdb6/input.json`
- `checks/audit/ed658816cdb6/racket.json`
- `checks/audit/ed658816cdb6/rival.json`

The Racket apply record binds the finding to generator SHA `1d3f02353a49755d879b19e17a826de62c53416562854c5dd18db4e848826371`, executed rule hash `84a3aadb879c`, and rule text SHA `b310229a0a580ae7af3295c155e71a5451e8768e17b24f2d4fc2dcbb52bf4847`.

Separately, the shared override stage reports more than twelve thousand blocking findings, including silent/mismatched exact controls and omitted keyed provenance, plus 17,700 legacy undeclared incompatibility warnings (`checks/audit-ed658-override/checks/ed658816cdb6_after_override.log`). Those contract failures reinforce that the generator is not ready, but the metric counterexample alone is a concrete data-quality defect.

No audit-target source was changed, as required by the assignment.
